scope: Theorem 6.1 (Annular-chain sewing) of the manuscript “Every complex K3 surface is Oka” (preprints/Every-complex-K3-surface-is-Oka-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 042 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c35e20c01dcefe76), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 31-32. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let M be a complex surface with a nowhere-zero holo- morphic two-form ω. Fix 0 < h < 1/8, r > 0, and A < ∞. For each j ∈ Z, let Lj ≥ 1 and let ϕj : {−2h < Y < Lj + 2h} × ∆r −→ M be a holomorphic map with ϕ∗ j ω = ω0. Suppose there are holomorphic translations Jj(w, p) = (w + aj(p), p), | Im aj(p) + Lj| < h/8, |a′ j(p)| ≤ A, and exact symplectic transitions Fj on Sj(h, r) = {|Y − Lj| < h} × ∆r such that ϕj = ϕj+1 ◦ Fj. Write J−1 j Fj = (w + uj, p + vj). Assume these lifts exist and supj ∥(uj, vj)∥Sj(h,r) ≤ e. 31 There are b > 0 and e∗ > 0, depending only on h, r, A and the indicated margins, such that, if e < e∗, these charts give a holomorphic symplectic immersion Φ : C × ∆b −→ M which is periodic of period one in the first variable. On a smaller domain in every original block, with fixed positive margins at both ends, Φ is obtained from ϕj by a small periodic symplectic change of variables. The corrected transitions are (w, p) 7−→ (w + e aj(p), p). The changes of variables and e aj −aj, together with any fixed finite number of derivatives on further smaller domains, tend uniformly to zero as e → 0. None of these assertions requires an upper bound for the Lj or a bound on the number of blocks.
